triage.note: D10 defect 4, postmortem shape S3. The three input modes each rendered `<button id="go-…">Extract</button>`: role `button`, accessible name "Extract", three times. Any plan targeting the button resolves to 3 matches — the ambiguity failure the browser-agent repo's M38 exists for. Red against the pre-D10 file (3cdfbf4), re-measured with the current check, three failures, one per button: `#go-fx: no accessible name of its own — all three modes read "Extract", which is the 3-match ambiguity (it carries neither aria-label nor aria-labelledby)`, and the same message for `#go-up` and `#go-url`. Green once each carries a distinct aria-label (fixture / uploaded file / EDGAR URL). The VISIBLE label stays "Extract" on all three deliberately — that is what the button does in every mode; the mode is what differs, and that is what the accessible name now says. PR #55 R3 found that distinctness was the WHOLE check, and distinctness is not correctness: labelling #go-fx "Upload" and #go-up "Fixture" keeps three distinct non-empty names and passed at invariant 63/63 = 1.000, while an accessibility-first reader picking by name then lands in the file-upload mode when it asked for the fixture — worse than the ambiguity the row set out to remove. Two clauses were added and both go red on exactly that mutation: each name must carry the substring naming its OWN mode, and each name must contain the button's own VISIBLE text (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name, which is what keeps a speech-input user's "click Extract" working once an aria-label is in play). The second clause is the one that makes this case back the row's 'screen-reader correctness, not agent special-casing' claim rather than merely asserting it. Red on that mutation, re-measured, four failures quoted whole: `#go-fx: accessible name 'Upload' does not name its own mode ('fixture') — distinct names that point at the wrong mode are worse than no names`; `#go-fx: accessible name 'Upload' does not contain its visible label 'Extract' (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name — speech input targets the word the user can see)`; `#go-up: accessible name 'Fixture' does not name its own mode ('upload') — distinct names that point at the wrong mode are worse than no names`; `#go-up: accessible name 'Fixture' does not contain its visible label 'Extract' (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name — speech input targets the word the user can see)`.

provenance: D10, created 2026-08-26 before the ARIA fix, per hard rule 2; per-mode and Label-in-Name clauses added in the PR #55 round-1 repair, red-first on the reviewer's own swapped-label mutation. Every output quoted above was pasted from a run observed during the round-2 repair (PR #55 R10 asked for exactly this audit): the pre-D10 red was re-measured with the current check, and the four mutation failures are now quoted whole rather than truncated mid-message as an earlier revision of this note had them.
